items.title: 68429_Walter P. Thomas oral history interview
items.q: I had one woman teacher, one female teacher, and one guy named McCord.

ctx.x: So when I went... I don't remember too much of the math I had in the seventh and eighth grades in Muskogee. So I talked my mother into letting me go off to school. A buddy of mine had gone to Wilberforce, came back and told me how good it was going off to school. So I found out about this school in Topeka, so I talked my mother into sending me there. My father wanted me to wait a year later. But my mother said, "Don't worry about it. You go on."

So I did. I went and made that... I started almost like you do it in college. I started in my freshman year. And how I got ahold of all them good teachers, I'll never know. I had one woman teacher, one female teacher, and one guy named McCord. He had a knot on his head. And we always thought all that knowledge was up there in that knot. And they were... To me they were so great, because the one thing they told us in the freshman class, he said, "Algebra is only arithmetic in algebraic form." Well, I had my…
